title: Gulf War
summary: Iraq invaded and annexed Kuwait on 2 August 1990; the Security Council, with the Soviet Union no longer vetoing, authorised the use of force, and a coalition of some forty states under American command destroyed the Iraqi army in Kuwait in six weeks of bombing and a hundred hours of ground fighting. The war stopped at the border: Saddam Hussein was left in power and put down the risings that followed. What was left behind — sanctions, two no-fly zones, a disarmament inspectorate and American forces in Saudi Arabia — is the arrangement that the next twelve years of the region were argued about, and that the war of 2003 was fought to end.
